about: The English meaning of N. Balasubramanian's सार्थ बिल्वाष्टकम् on sanskritdocuments.org (doc_shiva/bilva8mean.html), from the owner's printout: each verse's “Meaning of the verse” (for śloka 1, the translation given after its word meanings). Only typos are fixed (reconciliation.md).

m.sh1: I offer to Lord Shiva cluster of three bilva leaves which stand for three gunas that make up His Maya shakti, which represent His three eyes, the three kinds of weapons He bears and whose very thought or uttering of names destroys one's accumulated sins.
m.sh2: I perform puja to Lord Shiva with bunch of bilva leaves that are auspicious, soft and tender, have three leaves, which are not damaged or defective in any manner.
m.sh3: By offering puja to Shiva - Lord of Nandi - with bilva leaf that is whole and without defects one is freed from all sins.
m.sh4: If one gifts a sacred saligrama piece to a brahmin who has acquired the knowledge of Self, he earns great merit equal to that of performing a sacrifice.
m.sh5: Gifting of thousands of elephants or performing great sacrifices like the Vajapeya or gifting of young unmarried girls in marriage cannot be compared with the offering of a cluster of bilva leaves to Lord Shiva.
m.sh6: I offer the bilva tree that sprung from the body of LakShmi Devi and is dear to Lord Mahadeva.
m.sh7: Even having a look at the bilva tree or touching it destroys the most horrible sins one might have committed.
m.kashi: If one stays at the holy city of Kasi, then has darsan of the Lord Kalabhairava there, visits Prayag and has darsan of Lord Madhava there and also offers worship to Lord Shiva with bilva leaf he is assured of Lord's grace.
m.sh8: Worshipping Lord Shiva with a leaf from the bilva tree which represents Brahma, the creator in the root portion, Vishnu, the sustainer in the middle portion and Shiva, the destroyer in the top portion one can derive the supreme benefit.
m.phala: Whoever reads these sacred verses of Bilvashtakam in the proximity of Lord Shiva will be freed of all sins and attain the abode of Lord Shiva.
